findings.source: MultiSig.sol:249 for (uint256 i = 0; i < len;) { if (signers[i] == address(0)) revert InvalidSigner(i); ... if (validSigs == $.threshold) break; } return validSigs == $.threshold;
findings.issue: The loop is found but rotated: the printed condition is the in-body zero-signer test (or True), the real bound i < len is tested at the bottom of every arm next to a duplicated 'return threshold == u', and the code after the loop is the InvalidSigner revert, so the loop reads as 'while the signer is non-zero'.
findings.rule: When a loop's header block only tests a body condition whose failure leaves the loop to a revert, and the back edge is guarded by 'i + 1 < n' whose failure leads to the same code as the loop exit of the source form, re-rotate to 'while i < n' (the entry test is implied by the dominating 'n != 0' check) and keep the zero test as an 'if ... revert' in the body.
findings.verified: reading only (text_check passes on this contract, so the rotation is exact on the sampled paths)

findings.decompiled: def storage (vyper): stor0 is fixed array of mapping of uint256 at storage 0 ... storA70A is mapping of fixed array of struct of 1 slot at storage 0xa70a.. / stor0[address(cd[32 * idx + _param1 + 36])][sha3(0xa70a07de.., Bytes(4, 0x978aab92))] = uint95(storA70A[concat(Bytes(4, 0x978aab92))][0].field_1) + 1 / stor[sha3(_101, sha3(0xa70a07de.., Bytes(4, 0x978aab92)))]
findings.source: solady EnumerableSetLib: rootSlot = keccak256(set.slot . _ENUMERABLE_ADDRESS_SET_SLOT_SEED) and the position slot keccak256(value . rootSlot) (EtherFiSafe is solc 0.8.28, not Vyper)
findings.issue: The layout is declared Vyper because the root-slot hash puts the slot before the 4-byte seed; the Solidity-order position mapping keccak(value . rootSlot) is then printed either as raw stor[sha3(...)] (263 lines) or as stor0[value][rootSlot], a fixed array of mappings at slot 0 that does not exist (73 lines).
findings.rule: Decide the hash convention per access, not per contract: keccak(k . s) with s a slot expression is the mapping s[k] and keccak(s . c) with s a slot and c a short constant is a derived slot; never invent a base slot 0 to make keccak(x . y) fit 'array at 0, then mapping'.

notes: The pack resolved almost no internal functions for this contract (inheritance EtherFiSafe -> EtherFiSafeCore -> MultiSig/ModuleManager/RecoveryManager, libraries ArrayDeDupLib, SignatureUtils, solady EnumerableSetLib), so the reached code was read from the sources directly. 14 source loops, all present as whiles: EtherFiSafeCore:62 (initialize), :123 (getAdmins), :206 (execTransactionFromModule), ModuleManager:70, :106, :151, MultiSig:95, :249 (checkSignatures, rotated: first finding), :337 (_currentOwner, inlined in the 11 owner-gated functions), RecoveryManager:225 (recoverSafe), :300 (getRecoverySigners), ArrayDeDupLib:28 and :31 (nested, inlined for every array with more than one element), solady values():611. Solady's 'for {} 1 {} { ... break }' blocks in length/contains/add/remove always break in their first iteration, have no back edge, and are correctly shown as straight-line code (not counted). MultiSig:95 and ModuleManager:70 appear rotated after the duplicate check ('while idx + 1 < cd[..]', first iteration peeled: P3, 5 places). ~60 ABI-encoding loops (address[] cleanup, bool[] cleanup, bytes[] encoding) for calls and events stay whiles (P7). Large functions (configureOwners 1680 lines, setUserRecoverySigners 1390, configureModules 1180) reviewed by structure; checkSignatures, cancelNonce, execTransactionFromModule, initialize and getAdmins in detail. Faithful details checked: emit AccountRecovered($.incomingOwner) after the delete prints 'log ..: 0' as the source does; the tstore/tload of MODULE_BATCH_SLOT and its restore; ECDSA tryRecover error codes. P4: the set root is printed as storX[concat(Bytes(4, 0x978aab92))] (1168 lines). P8: keccak scratch writes around every set access and around tstore. Selector/event names are mostly unknown (not in the signature database).
summary: Faithful and every loop is present, but the signature loop is rotated so its condition reads as a zero-signer test, the storage is declared Vyper and Solady set positions appear as a fictitious array at slot 0 or raw hashes, and inside loops custom errors, ERC-1271 calls and two-array arguments lose their structure.
